tutorial.title: Looping Over Arrays
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to loop over arrays inside of functions.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's learn how to use functions to go over arrays and manipulate their values whenever we want, like when we click a button.

Run the code below that checks whether the value 66 exists in the grades array using a function.

lessons.title: Single Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
Functions are useful when we want to execute reusable code.

To access array elements using the searchGrade function, let's pass the grades array when calling the function.

Make sure to type grades.

lessons.title: Multiple Parameters
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to access elements stored in multiple arrays using the same function, we pass the arrays as arguments when calling the function.

Let's code the second array grades2 when calling searchGrade().

Make sure to pick ,, followed by grades2.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we want to access elements stored in multiple arrays using the same function, we pass the arrays as arguments when calling the function.

Call searchGrade() with the two grade arrays in the same order as its parameters.

Make sure to pick searchGrade, followed by grades, and finally grades2.

lessons.title: For loop
lessons.interactiveContent:
Once we've passed an array to a function, we can iterate over the array elements. Create a for loop to iterate through all grades elements.

Make sure to pick for, followed by (, and finally ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Once we've passed an array to a function, we can iterate over the array elements.

Complete the loop so it starts at the first grade, stops before len, and advances one index at a time.

Make sure to pick for, followed by i < len, and finally i++.

lessons.title: For Loop II
lessons.interactiveContent:
To retrieve each array element inside a for loop, we use the syntax array[i], where i is the current iteration, and array is the array name.

Let's write the code to retrieve individual grades elements.

Make sure to type grades[i].

lessons.title: Array and a Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
By using a function, an array, and another parameter, we can do a lot.

For example, let's search for the element 66 in the grades array by passing grades and then search to the searchGrade function.

Make sure to pick grades, followed by ,, and finally search.
lessons.hardModeContent:
By using a function, an array, and another parameter, we can do a lot.

Find the first grade equal to search, print the message, and stop scanning once it is found.

Make sure to pick grades[i], followed by ===, search, and finally break.

lessons.title: Multiple Arrays
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also use multiple arrays with a function to perform a specific action, such as finding common array elements.

Let's find common elements in two arrays by passing them to the compareArrays function.

Make sure to type one, two.

lessons.title: Question: Single Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we access array elements from within a function?

We pass the array to the functionWe call the array directly without passing it to the function

We pass the array to the function.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You have const prices = [99, 129] and function displayPrices(items).

Which call passes the array into items?

displayPrices(prices)displayPrices("prices")prices(displayPrices)

Make sure to pick displayPrices(prices).

lessons.title: Question: Multiple Parameters
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

It displays multiple arraysIt displays only the first array

It displays multiple arrays.
lessons.hardModeContent:
How many separate values does the function log when it is called?

Two arrays, one from each parameter.One combined array.Only the array of names.

Two arrays, one from each parameter.

lessons.title: Question: For loop
lessons.interactiveContent:
What can we use within a function to iterate over an array passed to the function?

We can use a for loop We can use an if statement

We can use a for loop .
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use a for loop within a function to iterate over an array passed to the function.

Inside a function, you need to visit each element of an array in order. Which structure fits that job?

A for loop.An if statement.A function call with no arguments.

A for loop.

lessons.title: Question: For loop II
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we use names[i] within a for loop like in the function below?

We retrieve array elements one by oneWe retrieve array elements all at once

We retrieve array elements one by one.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we use names[i] within a for loop like in the function below, we retrieve array elements one by one.

On the first loop pass, what does names[i] refer to?

The first element, "Mary".Both names at the same time.The length of the array.

The first element, "Mary".

lessons.title: Question: Array and a Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

It does not display anythingIt displays The name exists!

It does not display anything.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The loop compares each name with "June". What is logged if neither stored name matches?

Nothing is logged.The name exists! is logged.The loop logs both names automatically.

Nothing is logged.

lessons.title: Question: Multiple Arrays
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we pass multiple arrays to a function?

To perform a specific action that includes information from multiple arraysTo perform a specific action that includes information from only one array

To perform a specific action that includes information from multiple arrays.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You have two arrays, prices and discounts, and a function compare(costs, rates).

Which call passes prices into costs and discounts into rates?

compare(prices, discounts)compare("prices", "discounts")compare(discounts, prices)

compare(prices, discounts).

lessons.title: Example: Single Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
When calling the displayPrices function, code the value to display the prices array.

Make sure to type (prices).

lessons.title: Example: Multiple Parameters
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the prices and discounts arrays by passing them to the searchDiscount function.

Make sure to pick prices, followed by ,, and finally discounts.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Display the prices and discounts arrays by passing them to the searchDiscount function.

Complete the call with the array that contains prices first and the array that contains discount rates second.

Make sure to pick searchDiscount, followed by prices, and finally discounts.

lessons.title: Example: For loop
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make the code iterate over all prices elements.

Make sure to pick for, followed by (, and finally ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make the code iterate over all prices elements.

Use the array length as the stopping boundary and advance i after each price.

Make sure to pick for, followed by i < prices.length, and finally i++.

lessons.title: Example: For loop II
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the value that retrieves each array element from prices.

Make sure to pick prices, followed by [i].
lessons.hardModeContent:
Code the value that retrieves each array element from prices.

Print the price at the current index, not the index number or the whole array.

Make sure to pick i++, followed by console.log, and finally prices[i].

lessons.title: Example: Array and a Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
To perform a specific operation to array elements, pass prices and discount to applyDiscount().

The output in the console will contain discount values for prices.

Make sure to pick ( followed by prices and then ,, discount, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
To perform a specific operation to array elements, pass prices and discount to applyDiscount().

Multiply each price by the discount rate. Put the price on the left and the rate on the right.

Make sure to pick i++, followed by console.log, prices[i], *, and finally discount.

lessons.title: Example: Multiple Arrays
lessons.interactiveContent:
To calculate discount values based on different discounts, pass both prices and discounts arrays to getValues().

Make sure to type prices, discounts.
